speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details, Mrs. [Name]. You mentioned a 1-month history of nonproductive cough and shortness of breath that worsens with exertion and at night. Do you have any history of asthma, allergies, or heart disease? Additionally, have you noticed wheezing, chest tightness, or any changes in your sputum color during this time?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious bronchial hyperreactivity with residual airway inflammation.

Your previous doctor's suggestion of pyelonephritis is incorrect, as that is an infection of the kidney which does not typically present with episodic cough and shortness of breath triggered by exertion. To confirm the nature of the airway inflammation and rule out other causes like asthma or pneumonia, I need to see your lung status.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Spirometry
